phys_3_2 G1.issue: Four lessons (3, 7, 9, 11) held a full practical plus calculations and could not fit 40 minutes: now 80-minute double periods. Unit total recomputed (880 min = 22 periods, matching KICD's 22 lessons); lessons 4, 10 and 12 get minute-by-minute pacing. Lesson 3 asks for an ammeter practical at four points in series, a parallel demonstration, I = Q/t calculations, a CER statement, the Driving Question Board and a model revision. That cannot fit 40 minutes, and the old text itself recommended a double lesson. The teacher must decide: keep it as one 80-minute double period (suggested) or keep 40 minutes and make the parallel readings a teacher demonstration only. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL 80 minutes (2 x 40-minute periods)

phys_3_2-022.issue: Ordinary 5 A fuse wire needs several amperes to melt. A pack of six dry cells cannot supply that, so the demonstration as written would probably not work. A single thin strand of steel wool, the usual low-voltage demonstration, breaks at about an ampere or less. Teachers should check their own equipment before the lesson. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Mr. Otieno connects a single thin strand of steel wool (ordinary 5 A fuse wire needs several amperes, which a dry-cell pack cannot supply) in series with a 9 V supply and a bulb bank, then increases the number of parallel bulbs until the strand glows and breaks.

phys_3_2 G12.issue: Added Kiswahili term supports where new words first appear (Lessons 2, 5, 11): the words are suggestions for a Kiswahili-speaking teacher to confirm. The sequence had no language support for English learners and no Kiswahili. A short routine is added where the circuit words first appear: each word is written in English with a Kiswahili equivalent beside it, and learners add the word they use at home. The Kiswahili words are suggestions that a Kiswahili-speaking teacher must confirm before use. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Correct only vocabulary, such as using 'open circuit' for a broken loop. Language support: write each new term on the board in English with a Kiswahili word beside it and invite learners to add the word they use at home. Suggested words (a Kiswahili-speaking teacher to confirm): circuit = saketi; series = mfululizo; parallel = sambamba; battery = betri; switch = swichi.

phys_3_2-051.issue: KICD content and outcomes that this 12-lesson sequence does not teach or assess: internal resistance and E = I(R + r) (outcome b); resistivity as a quantity and 'various methods' of finding resistance, including resistor colour codes, the Wheatstone bridge and the metre bridge (outcome b and content); classifying conductors as ohmic or non-ohmic (only touched on in Lesson 5); the 'applications of resistors' content beyond heater elements and fuse wire. KICD allocates 22 lessons to this sub-strand and this sequence has 12 lessons (22 periods once double lessons are counted), so no lessons can be added here. Suggestion: teachers decide whether to add short extensions (for example internal resistance in Lesson 9 with the cells, resistivity rho = RA/L in Lesson 6, colour codes as homework in Lesson 5) or accept the gap. Strand and sub-strand numbers (3.0 and 3.2) and the name 'Current Electricity' match KICD. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL No text was changed. The suggestion, if any, is in the issue text above.
